vocabulary.note_ar: تُكتب في الرسائل غير الرسمية فقط، وفي الكتابة الرسمية اكتب going to
vocabulary.note_en: Use it in speech and casual texts only; write "going to" in formal writing.

vocabulary.note_ar: لا تُستخدم مع he/she: نقول he wants to
vocabulary.note_en: Not with he/she: say "he wants to".

vocabulary.meaning_en: fast spoken form of "have got to" (must)
fast spoken form of "kind of" (a little)
fast spoken form of "a lot of"
vocabulary.example: I have a lotta work today.

vocabulary.meaning_en: fast spoken form of "I don't know"
fast spoken form of "what are you" / "what have you"
fast spoken form of "what do you"

vocabulary.note_en: The sounds d + y join and sound like "j".

vocabulary.example: I'm kind of busy right now.

fine_lines.title: gonna vs wanna vs gotta
fine_lines.explanation_ar: gonna = going to (سوف). wanna = want to (أريد). gotta = have got to (يجب). ثلاث كلمات متشابهة في الصوت لكن معانيها مختلفة.
fine_lines.explanation_en: gonna = going to (future). wanna = want to (wish). gotta = have got to (must). They sound similar but mean different things.

fine_lines.title: won't vs want
fine_lines.explanation_ar: won't = will not (لن) وتُنطق /woʊnt/ مثل don't. want = يريد وتُنطق /wɒnt/. انتبه للفرق في الصوت.
fine_lines.explanation_en: "Won't" = will not, said /woʊnt/ like "don't". "Want" = wish, said /wɒnt/.

fine_lines.title: can vs can't
fine_lines.explanation_ar: في الكلام السريع can تُنطق ضعيفة /kən/، وcan't تُنطق قوية وأطول /kænt/ أو /kɑːnt/، وغالبًا لا تُسمع t.
fine_lines.explanation_en: In fast speech "can" is weak /kən/; "can't" is strong and longer, and the t is often not heard.

expressions.example: I bought a new bag. Whaddaya think?
Hey, whatcha doing? - Just reading.

expressions.meaning_en: A greeting; in fast speech "are you" becomes "aya".
expressions.example: Hi Sam, howaya?
D'you wanna go to the park?
Didja eat the cake?
Wouldja like some tea?
I'm gonna visit my aunt this weekend.
I wanna see the mountains again.
I gotta finish my homework.

expressions.meaning_en: Suggesting we leave or start together.
expressions.example: Come on, let's go!

expressions.meaning_en: Talking about the past that didn't happen.
expressions.example: I'd've helped you if you'd asked.
Don't go there, it's dangerous.
I'm full. I can't eat this.

expressions.meaning_en: Saying you refuse in the future.
expressions.example: Sorry, I won't do it again.
I haven't seen her today.
Sorry, he isn't here right now.
Where's the remote? - Dunno.

expressions.phrase: I don't know what to do.
expressions.meaning_en: I have no idea what to do next.
expressions.example: My phone is broken. I don't know what to do.

expressions.phrase: I'm out of here. (I'm outta here)
expressions.example: Work is done. I'm outta here!
Can we talk later? I'm kinda busy.

expressions.phrase: I have a lot of work. (a lotta)
expressions.example: I can't come. I have a lotta work.

expressions.meaning_en: Asking someone to hand you something (casual).
expressions.example: Gimme that book, please.

grammar.title: Contractions with not: don't, can't, won't, haven't, isn't
grammar.explanation_ar: نختصر not مع الفعل المساعد: do not = don't، cannot = can't، will not = won't، have not = haven't، is not = isn't. الاختصار طبيعي في الكلام، والصيغة الكاملة أقوى أو أكثر رسمية.
grammar.explanation_en: We join "not" to a helping verb: do not = don't, cannot = can't, will not = won't, have not = haven't, is not = isn't. Short forms are normal in speech; full forms are stronger or more formal.

grammar.title: Fast speech: gonna, wanna, gotta
grammar.explanation_ar: في الكلام السريع يدمج الأمريكيون الكلمات: going to = gonna، want to = wanna، have got to = gotta. تعلمها لتفهم الأجانب، لكن في الكتابة الرسمية اكتب الصيغة الكاملة.
grammar.explanation_en: In fast speech words join: going to = gonna, want to = wanna, have got to = gotta. Learn them to understand natives, but write the full form in formal writing.
examples: I'm gonna visit my aunt. = I'm going to visit my aunt.
I wanna eat pizza. = I want to eat pizza.
I gotta go. = I have got to go.

grammar.title: Let's + verb
grammar.explanation_ar: Let's اختصار let us، ونستخدمها لاقتراح فعل شيء معًا. بعدها فعل أصلي.
grammar.explanation_en: "Let's" = let us. Use it to suggest doing something together. Follow it with a base verb.
examples: Let's give someone else a chance.

grammar.title: Linking sounds: d + y = j, t + y = ch
grammar.explanation_ar: عندما تأتي كلمة تنتهي بـ d قبل you يندمج الصوتان ويصبحان "ج": did you = didja، would you = wouldja. وt + you تصبح "تش": what are you = whatcha.
grammar.explanation_en: When d comes before "you", the sounds join into "j": did you = didja, would you = wouldja. t + you becomes "ch": whatcha.
examples: Would you like tea? = Wouldja like tea?
What are you doing? = Whatcha doing?
